dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For N natural and omega in Omega, Z_N(omega) is (sigma times sqrt(N)) inverse multiplied by the sum over i=0,...,N-1 of X_i(omega)-m.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the normalized centered partial sum whose upper-tail law is compared with the standard normal law.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: If every X_i is almost-everywhere measurable, then Z_N is almost-everywhere measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the measurability needed to form the pushforward probability law of Z_N and imposes no additional probabilistic hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: C is the fixed real constant (1/pi)*(1+pi^2/32)*((1/6)*M_2+(1/8)*M_3)+2*sqrt(2*pi), with M_k defined by D009.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the explicit multiplicative coefficient on the right-hand side; the asserted bound uses this fixed C, not coefficient one.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: Omega is an arbitrary measurable space and mu is a probability measure on it.
X is a natural-number-indexed sequence of real random variables, and m and sigma are real numbers.
N is universally quantified over natural numbers with 1<=N, and t over all real thresholds.
hypotheses: The family X_i is mutually independent under mu.
Every X_i has the same distribution as X_0 under mu.
The integral of X_0 is m and its variance is sigma^2.
conclusions: For every N>=1 and real t, abs(Law(Z_N)([t,infinity))-StandardNormalLaw([t,infinity))) <= C*((integral |X_0-m|^3 dmu)/sigma^3)/sqrt(N).
mathematical_definitions: Law(Z_N) is the pushforward of mu by Z_N and StandardNormalLaw is gaussianReal 0 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Every identically distributed, mutually independent real-valued sequence on a probability space with finite third moments, common mean m, and positive common standard deviation sigma satisfies a uniform-in-threshold upper-tail normal-approximation estimate for each positive sample size N. The normalized centered sum uses X_0 through X_{N-1}, and the error is bounded by the fixed explicit constant C times the standardized third absolute centered moment at rate 1/sqrt(N).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The variables use zero-based indexing and Z_N sums exactly X_0 through X_{N-1}.
The restriction N>=1 excludes the empty sum and division by sqrt(0).
The strict sigma>0 assumption makes both normalizations nondegenerate.
The L^3 hypotheses make the third moments finite and supply almost-everywhere measurability.
The event is the inclusive upper ray [t,infinity).
The right-hand side uses the fixed explicit C rather than coefficient one.
Positive-variance iid sequences with finite third moment show the hypotheses are not inherently contradictory.
ambiguities: Measure.real uses ENNReal.toReal, but probability-law set masses are finite and represent ordinary real probabilities.
No claim is made about optimality or numerical simplification of C.
The statement compares upper-tail probabilities pointwise rather than directly naming a supremum metric.
